quests.instruction: A banana is green and firm at the shop. What will happen as it ripens?
quests.correctAnswer: It turns yellow and gets softer
options: It turns yellow and gets softer
It turns blue and gets harder
It stays green and gets smaller
quests.hint: Think about the banana you usually eat.
quests.explanation: As a banana ripens, its starches turn into sugars, the peel turns yellow and the fruit gets softer and sweeter.
quests.funFact: Bananas are usually shipped green and ripened in special rooms near the shops.

quests.instruction: A yellow banana has small brown spots. What does that usually mean?
quests.correctAnswer: It is very ripe and sweet
options: It is still unripe
It is very ripe and sweet
It has never been washed
quests.hint: Think about what happens as a banana gets older.
quests.explanation: Small brown spots show a banana is very ripe, soft and sweet.
quests.funFact: Very ripe bananas are great for baking because they are sweet and easy to mash.

quests.instruction: Most tomatoes start out green. Which color change shows a red tomato is ripening?
quests.correctAnswer: Green to red
options: Red to green
Blue to purple
Green to red
quests.hint: Think of a tomato on a plant.
quests.explanation: A red tomato slowly changes from green to red as it ripens.
quests.funFact: Tomatoes ripen faster in warm weather.

quests.instruction: Which clue shows a Hass avocado is ready to eat?
quests.correctAnswer: Dark skin that gives slightly when pressed gently
options: Bright green skin that feels hard as a rock
Dark skin that gives slightly when pressed gently
Skin that feels wet and slippery all over
quests.hint: Think about both color and feel.
quests.explanation: A ripe Hass avocado turns dark and gives a little under gentle pressure.
quests.funFact: Avocados do not ripen on the tree, only after they are picked.

quests.instruction: Where do you press gently on a pear to check if it is ripe?
quests.correctAnswer: Near the stem, at the narrow top
options: At the widest part, as hard as you can
Near the stem, at the narrow top
At the very bottom, with a fingernail
quests.hint: Pears soften from the inside out.
quests.explanation: Pears ripen from the inside out, so a gentle press near the stem tells you more than squeezing the middle.
quests.funFact: Pressing hard leaves bruises, so a gentle thumb is best.

quests.instruction: How can you gently check whether a kiwi is ready to eat?
quests.correctAnswer: It gives slightly under a gentle squeeze
options: It gives slightly under a gentle squeeze
It feels as hard as a rock when squeezed
It feels very soft and wet all over
quests.hint: Ripe does not mean mushy.
quests.explanation: A ripe kiwi gives slightly under gentle pressure but is not mushy.
quests.funFact: Kiwis ripen faster when they sit near ripe apples or bananas.

quests.instruction: Which clue suggests a pineapple may be ready to eat?
quests.correctAnswer: A sweet smell near the bottom
options: A sharp, fermented smell near the top
No smell at all near the bottom
A sweet smell near the bottom
quests.hint: Sniff near the base.
quests.explanation: A sweet, fruity smell at the base is a good sign. A sour or fermented smell can mean it is past its best.
quests.funFact: A pineapple does not get sweeter once it is picked, though it can get softer.

quests.instruction: What can tell you a mango is ripe?
quests.correctAnswer: A fruity smell near the stem and a slight give
options: A fruity smell near the stem and a slight give
A smell like wet paper and a very hard feel
Cracked skin and a sour, fermented smell
quests.hint: Color alone can be misleading.
quests.explanation: Ripe mangoes smell sweet near the stem and give slightly when pressed gently. Skin color varies by kind.
quests.funFact: Many mangoes are ripened at room temperature in a paper bag.

quests.instruction: An orange feels heavy for its size. What does that often mean?
quests.correctAnswer: It is full of juice
options: It is full of juice
It is empty inside
It is still a flower
quests.hint: Water is heavy.
quests.explanation: Oranges that feel heavy for their size usually hold more juice.
quests.funFact: Citrus fruit does not ripen further after picking, so it is picked when ready.

quests.instruction: Which clue helps you choose a ripe watermelon?
quests.correctAnswer: A creamy-yellow patch where it rested on the ground
options: A bright white patch where it rested on the ground
A shiny green patch where it rested on the ground
A creamy-yellow patch where it rested on the ground
quests.hint: Look at the spot that touched the soil.
quests.explanation: The creamy-yellow field spot shows the melon spent enough time on the ground to ripen. A white spot can mean it was picked too soon.
quests.funFact: Many people also tap a watermelon and listen for a deep, hollow sound.

quests.instruction: A ripe cantaloupe often has a smooth, round scar where the stem was. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: It slipped off the vine easily when ready
options: It was snipped off the vine with scissors
It grew a small hole where the stem was
It slipped off the vine easily when ready
quests.hint: Think about a fruit letting go of its plant.
quests.explanation: Cantaloupes that are ready come away from the vine on their own, leaving a smooth scar.
quests.funFact: Farmers call this easy separation from the vine a slip.

quests.instruction: Which clue shows grapes are fresh?
quests.correctAnswer: Plump and firmly attached to green stems
options: Wrinkled and loosely attached to brown stems
Plump and firmly attached to green stems
Soft and sticky with juice leaking out
quests.hint: Fresh grapes look full and healthy.
quests.explanation: Fresh grapes are plump and firm and stay attached to green stems.
quests.funFact: Grapes are usually sold in bunches that are still attached to their stems.

quests.instruction: Which of these will not get sweeter after it is picked?
quests.correctAnswer: Strawberry
options: Banana
Avocado
Strawberry
quests.hint: Two of these keep ripening on the counter.
quests.explanation: Strawberries are picked when ripe and do not sweeten further, while bananas and avocados continue to ripen.
quests.funFact: That is why strawberries are picked when they are mostly red.

quests.instruction: A pear is hard at the shop. How can you help it ripen?
quests.correctAnswer: Leave it on the counter at room temperature
options: Leave it on the counter at room temperature
Put it in the freezer for a day or two
Soak it in warm water for a whole day
quests.hint: Think about warmth and patience.
quests.explanation: Many pears are sold firm and ripen at room temperature over a few days.
quests.funFact: Once a pear is ripe, the fridge can slow down further ripening.

quests.instruction: A hard avocado is put in a paper bag with a ripe banana. What happens?
quests.correctAnswer: It ripens faster
options: It stays hard forever
It ripens faster
It turns bright blue
quests.hint: Ripe fruit gives off an invisible gas.
quests.explanation: Ripe fruit gives off a natural gas called ethylene, and the bag keeps it close, so the avocado ripens faster.
quests.funFact: Ethylene is the same natural gas that helps fruit ripen on the plant.

quests.instruction: What usually happens to a fruit's taste as it ripens?
quests.correctAnswer: It gets sweeter and less sour
options: It gets sweeter and less sour
It gets more sour and less sweet
It loses most of its flavor
quests.hint: Think about biting into an unripe fruit and a ripe one.
quests.explanation: As many fruits ripen, starches turn into sugars and sour acids fade, so the fruit tastes sweeter.
quests.funFact: Many fruits also change color, smell and softness as they ripen.

quests.instruction: Which fruit has a kind that feels dry and puckery in the mouth until it is very soft?
quests.correctAnswer: Persimmon
options: Banana
Cherries
Persimmon
quests.hint: This fruit has firm kinds and soft kinds.
quests.explanation: Hachiya persimmons are very puckery until they are soft and jelly-like, while Fuyu persimmons are sweet while still firm.
quests.funFact: Dried persimmons are a traditional treat in parts of East Asia.

quests.instruction: Which fruit is often shredded while still green and firm for a crunchy salad?
quests.correctAnswer: Papaya
options: Papaya
Peach
Plum
quests.hint: Think about a tropical fruit used like a vegetable.
quests.explanation: Green, unripe papaya is firm and mild, so it can be shredded into salads. Ripe papaya is soft and sweet.
quests.funFact: Green papaya salad is a famous dish in Southeast Asia.

quests.instruction: Which sign suggests a fruit is overripe?
quests.correctAnswer: It is very mushy, wrinkled or leaking juice
options: It is firm with smooth, shiny skin and no marks
It is very mushy, wrinkled or leaking juice
It has a fresh, sweet, fruity smell all over
quests.hint: Think about fruit that has been around too long.
quests.explanation: Fruit that is very mushy, wrinkled or leaking is past its best.
quests.funFact: Overripe fruit often attracts tiny fruit flies.

quests.instruction: You see fuzzy mold on one strawberry in a box. What is the best choice?
quests.correctAnswer: Throw that berry away and tell a grown-up
options: Cut around the mold and eat the rest
Throw that berry away and tell a grown-up
Wash that berry well and eat it
quests.hint: Think about what mold can do to nearby fruit.
quests.explanation: Mold can spread, so moldy fruit should be thrown away and a grown-up should check the other berries.
quests.funFact: Berries can mold quickly because their skin is thin and they hold a lot of moisture.

quests.instruction: An apple has a small bruise but is otherwise firm. What can a grown-up do?
quests.correctAnswer: Cut away the bruised spot and use the rest
options: Eat the bruised part without checking it
Wait until the whole apple is covered in mold
Cut away the bruised spot and use the rest
quests.hint: Only the damaged spot is a problem.
quests.explanation: A small bruise only spoils the spot where it is, so a grown-up can cut it away and use the rest.
quests.funFact: Bruises happen when fruit is dropped or squashed, which is why careful packing matters.

quests.instruction: How should cut fruit be stored?
quests.correctAnswer: In a covered container in the fridge
options: In an open bowl on the kitchen table
In a closed bag on a sunny shelf
In a covered container in the fridge
quests.hint: Cut fruit spoils faster than whole fruit.
quests.explanation: Cut fruit spoils faster than whole fruit, so keep it cold and covered and eat it soon.
quests.funFact: A whole watermelon can sit at room temperature for a few days, but cut pieces belong in the fridge.

quests.instruction: Why might you keep ripe bananas away from other fruit?
quests.correctAnswer: They give off a gas that makes nearby fruit ripen faster
options: They give off a gas that makes nearby fruit taste sour
They give off a gas that makes nearby fruit ripen faster
They give off cold air that slows nearby fruit down
quests.hint: Remember the paper bag trick.
quests.explanation: Ripe bananas give off ethylene, a gas that speeds up the ripening of fruit nearby.
quests.funFact: Apples also give off a lot of ripening gas.

quests.instruction: When is the best time to wash berries?
quests.correctAnswer: Just before you eat them
options: As soon as you get home, then store them wet
Never, because berries cannot be washed
Just before you eat them
quests.hint: Think about what extra moisture does.
quests.explanation: Moisture makes berries spoil faster, so rinse them just before you eat them.
quests.funFact: A paper towel in a berry container can soak up extra moisture.

quests.instruction: You have a soft, slightly bruised peach and a firm pear. Which should you eat first?
quests.correctAnswer: The soft peach, because it will spoil sooner
options: The soft peach, because it will spoil sooner
The firm pear, because it is the freshest
Whichever one is heavier, no matter what
quests.hint: Think about which one will spoil first.
quests.explanation: Soft, bruised fruit spoils sooner, so eat it first and give the firm pear a few more days.
quests.funFact: Eating the ripest fruit first helps cut down on food waste.

quests.instruction: What can you do with very ripe bananas that are too soft to eat plain?
quests.correctAnswer: Peel them and freeze them for smoothies
options: Peel them and freeze them for smoothies
Leave them in the sun to dry out slowly
Dry them on a shelf for a whole month
quests.hint: Think about creamy blended drinks.
quests.explanation: Very ripe bananas can be peeled, sliced and frozen to use in smoothies later.
quests.funFact: Frozen banana pieces blend into a thick, creamy treat.

quests.instruction: Why do many people keep tomatoes on the counter instead of in the fridge?
quests.correctAnswer: Cold can make them mealy and less flavorful
options: Cold makes them ripen far too quickly
Cold makes them too hard to ever slice
Cold can make them mealy and less flavorful
quests.hint: Think about how cold affects flavor.
quests.explanation: Cold can make tomatoes soft and mealy and dull their flavor, so many people keep ripe tomatoes at room temperature.
quests.funFact: Tomatoes taste best when they are fully ripe.

quests.instruction: A fruit that is not ready to eat yet is called what?
quests.correctAnswer: Unripe
options: Overripe
Unripe
Seedless
quests.hint: Think about the opposite of ripe.
quests.explanation: Unripe means not ready to eat yet. Overripe means past its best.
quests.funFact: Ripe fruit often smells sweeter than unripe fruit.

quests.instruction: A tomato at the shop is still pale green. What can help it ripen?
quests.correctAnswer: Leave it at room temperature for a few days
options: Put it in the freezer for a day
Leave it at room temperature for a few days
Wrap it tightly in plastic and chill it
quests.hint: Think about warmth and time.
quests.explanation: Tomatoes keep ripening after they are picked, and warmth helps them turn red.
quests.funFact: A pale tomato usually turns redder after a few days at room temperature.

quests.instruction: Which clue helps you choose a good pomegranate?
quests.correctAnswer: It feels heavy for its size with firm, deep-colored skin
options: It feels heavy for its size with firm, deep-colored skin
It feels light and hollow, with dull, pale, soft skin
It feels soft and squashy, with leaking, cracked skin
quests.hint: Think about juice and seeds.
quests.explanation: A heavy pomegranate with firm skin is usually full of juicy seeds.
quests.funFact: Pomegranates can keep well in a cool place for a long time.
